blogs.title: Ownership is Not Propensity: Navigating the Rule 404(b) Boundaries in Firearm Possession Cases
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Eighth Circuit's distinction between 'propensity' evidence and 'intrinsic' evidence under Federal Rule of Evidence 404(b). It explores how the court justified admitting testimony regarding the defendant's prior possession of a specific firearm to prove current ownership, and the implications this has for prosecutors seeking to establish a 'continuous possession' narrative in weapons charges.

blogs.title: When Guidelines Clash: The 'Greater Offense Level' Rule and the ACCA
blogs.description: A technical deep-dive into the sentencing mechanics of the Armed Career Criminal Act (ACCA). The post examines the interaction between the standard United States Sentencing Guidelines (USSG) and the ACCA, specifically focusing on the court’s application of the 'greater offense level' rule when a defendant qualifies for multiple sentencing enhancements, including the § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) firearm connection increase.

blogs.title: Contextualizing Hearsay: Judicial Discretion and the Confrontation Clause in Violent Crime Trials
blogs.description: This post explores the court's refusal to grant a limiting instruction regarding a victim's out-of-court statements to police. It discusses the tension between the Confrontation Clause and the government's interest in providing 'context' for police actions, and the Eighth Circuit's preference for judicial discretion and late-trial instructions over prophylactic limiting instructions.

blogs.title: The Shield of Substantial Evidence: The High Bar for Overturning Evidentiary Errors
blogs.description: Focusing on the 'substantial prejudice' standard, this post discusses how the Eighth Circuit handles multiple, albeit potentially erroneous, evidentiary rulings. It analyzes why a heavy burden of physical and testimonial evidence can insulate a conviction from reversal, even when a defendant raises several procedural and evidentiary objections on appeal.
